en: The Apadāna of the Elder Tiṇukkadhāriya from the Jagatidāyaka Chapter, the Fourth The Apadāna of the Elder Tiṇukkadhāriya: In the past, when the lifespan was twenty thousand years, the Buddha Kassapa appeared in the world. He was the Teacher of the Three Worlds, the All-Knowing One, the Fully Enlightened One, the one with the ten powers. At that time, I was a young man, a student of the Vedas; I was well-versed in the three Vedas and skilled in all branches of knowledge. Having heard of the Buddha’s fame, I went to the presence of the Sage. There I saw the Teacher, the Blessed One, the Fully Enlightened One. With palms joined together, I paid homage to the Great Hero; then I took a torch of grass and offered it to the Buddha. Having made this offering, I spoke these words to the Teacher: “May you, O Blessed One, accept this gift from me. The Teacher, the Great Sage, accepted my offering; having accepted it, he then spoke these words to me: “By this root of merit, may you attain the fruit of Buddhahood; may you become a Buddha, a teacher of gods and men. Having heard the words of the Buddha, I was filled with joy; I paid homage to the Teacher and departed from his presence. For eighty-four thousand years I practiced the holy life; I observed the five precepts and kept them perfectly pure. When the Blessed One Kassapa passed away, the relics were enshrined in a stūpa made of sandalwood. I built a stone platform for that stūpa, and upon that platform I established a parasol. Because of that deed, I have been reborn in heaven; for ninety-one aeons I have never fallen into the lower realms. Now, having reached the final birth, I am a disciple of the Buddha; I have attained the state of an Arhat, free from all defilements. Thus did the Elder Tiṇukkadhāriya speak of his own past deeds. This is the Apadāna of the Elder Tiṇukkadhāriya.
“With a clear heart and joyful mind, [I offered] to the supreme Bodhi tree of Padumuttara Buddha.”
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of giving firewood.
The defilements have been burnt away by me.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Elder Tiṇukkadhāriya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Tiṇukkadhāriya is the fourth.
